description: Single source of truth for AutoFlow's per-phase spawn policy (model + effort). Read it with scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh; never restate its values in prose (CLAUDE.md > Spawn Model — Phase-by-Phase).
sample_contract: This file is a SAMPLE carrying the values currently applied, not a universal vocabulary the framework enforces. It ships as a `scaffold` artifact: a stamp/install creates it only when absent and never overwrites it (not even under --force), so the values here are the target's to configure at stamp time and afterwards. On a version bump, run `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` and add any newly required row — the drift detector's D6 leg runs that check and the required-row comparison against the clone's sample at /autoflow:install and PREFLIGHT, so a stale scaffold is reported there with the rows to fix; both deliberation workflows fail closed on a missing required workflow_sites row. `check` reads the agent definitions from `.claude/agents/` when it holds autoflow-*.md files, otherwise from the installed plugin's agents/ (resolved via scripts/lib/plugin-root.sh: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a hook, the harness registries under ~/.claude/plugins in a plain shell) — a thin-root target has only the plugin copy; `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<plugin dir>` points it there explicitly. A phases[].effort is not a target-side lever: it must equal the `effort:` frontmatter line of the definition the target actually loads (the plugin's, on a thin-root target) and `check` fails closed otherwise — see effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership; a target that needs a different direct-spawn effort changes the shipped definition, not this row. workflow_sites effort stays target-configurable.

effort_contract.is_the_vocabulary_check_applies: `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` reads its admitted effort vocabulary and its inherit sentinel from THIS object. A runtime with a different effort vocabulary is accommodated by editing this contract, never by patching the checker; model values are not validated beyond presence and shape
effort_contract.admitted_one_spelling_per_level: this policy admits one spelling per level; the harness alias "med" for "medium" is not admitted here
effort_contract.sentinel_is_config_only: "inherit" is this file's own vocabulary and is never written to either harness channel: a Workflow agent() opts object omits the effort key, and an agent-definition frontmatter omits the effort line
effort_contract.absent_means: identical to "inherit" — the row declares no override and the spawn inherits the session effort. A row carrying no effort key at all is a validation error, not an inherit: `spawn-policy.sh check` rejects it
effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership: A phases[] row's effort is DELIVERED by the agent definition's `effort:` frontmatter line, not by this file. Phase-row effort is fixed per plugin version and is not a per-target lever; this file's phases[].effort is the projection source at the tool repository and must equal the loaded definition's line — `check` fails closed on a mismatch. Only workflow_sites effort reaches its spawn from this file at run time and is configurable per target. A row that uses a harness research type (Explore / Plan / claude-code-guide) admits the inherit sentinel only; `check` refuses a concrete effort there. The projection is recognised in one canonical spelling only — `effort: <value>` at column 0 of the first YAML block, unquoted, no trailing comment; any other spelling a YAML parser could read as that key — including an indented key — is refused by `check`. The block itself is accepted in block style only — one plain `key: value` per line at column 0, blank lines and `#` comments; a flow mapping, an explicit key, a merge key or a multi-line scalar is refused as a shape, before any "no effort line means inherit" verdict.

diagnose-intake-triage.work_type: new-issue readiness pre-filter (planning/design/ADR prerequisite), no code tools

diagnose-loopcheck.work_type: review-response loop check — prior-cycle complaint-class comparison

diagnose-phase-3.work_type: necessity scoring (Behavior gap + Code-change lever; reuse-neutral)

architect-dev-participant.work_type: ARCHITECT relay participant, Developer AI side — one persistent spawn per discussion, woken by agent ID for each of its turns; feature design under the Discussion Protocol

architect-test-participant.work_type: ARCHITECT relay participant, Test AI side — one persistent spawn per discussion, woken by agent ID for each of its turns; verification design under the Discussion Protocol

red.work_type: acceptance criteria → test code; test doubles re-derived from the real types and response shapes

green.work_type: minimum implementation that passes the tests

handoff-review-triage.work_type: reviewer-comment ingestion (severity classification) + Low-finding impact judgment
